candidates.name: Priya Raghavan
candidates.summary: Priya is a near-ideal match: 6 years of hands-on React/Node delivery with two production migrations she owned end-to-end. Her experience leading a 4-person pod maps directly to the team-lead expectations in the spec.
strengths: Led migration of a monolith to microservices serving 2M MAU — matches the spec's scaling requirement
Concrete metrics throughout the resume (cut p95 latency 40%, reduced infra spend 25%)
AWS certifications backed by actual architecture decisions, not just the cert list
red_flags: Two stints under 12 months in the last three years — worth probing reasons for leaving
No direct experience with the client's specific stack component (GraphQL federation)
screening_questions: Walk me through why you left CloudNine after 9 months — what would your manager there say?
The role uses GraphQL federation heavily. What's your closest hands-on experience to that?
You list 'led a pod of 4' — were you the people manager, the tech lead, or both?
What was the hardest production incident in the 2M MAU migration, and what did you personally do?
candidates.submittal_draft: Priya brings 6 years of full-stack delivery with a track record our client will recognize immediately: she led the decomposition of a 2M-MAU monolith into microservices, cutting p95 latency by 40% while mentoring a four-engineer pod. Her AWS depth is practical rather than certificate-deep, and she is available to interview this week. We rate her a strong fit for the Senior Full-Stack role and recommend moving directly to a technical interview.

candidates.name: Marcus Webb
candidates.summary: Marcus has the right keywords but thinner evidence of ownership — most bullets describe team accomplishments rather than his individual contribution. Could be a solid mid-level hire if the screening call surfaces specifics.
strengths: Relevant stack coverage (React, Node, Postgres) across 4 years
Startup background suggests comfort with ambiguity, which the client values
red_flags: Nearly every bullet starts with 'Worked on' or 'Participated in' — individual ownership unclear
Claims 'architected CI/CD pipeline' but lists no tooling specifics anywhere
Six-month employment gap in 2025 not addressed
screening_questions: Pick the project you're proudest of — what part of it exists only because of you?
You mention architecting a CI/CD pipeline. Which tools, and what did the pipeline look like before and after?
What were you doing between March and September 2025?
If I called your last tech lead, what would they say you're best and worst at?
candidates.submittal_draft: Marcus offers four years of full-stack experience across two early-stage startups, with working coverage of the client's core stack. He presents as a dependable mid-level engineer who has shipped in fast-moving environments. We recommend a screening call to validate depth of individual contribution before client submittal.

candidates.name: Candidate 3
candidates.summary: This resume is a keyword list with almost no evidence of delivered work — 14 frameworks claimed across 3 years of experience. Submitting this profile would risk the agency's credibility with the client.
strengths: Lists exposure to the required technologies, which may reflect bootcamp coverage
red_flags: 14 frameworks/languages claimed in 3 years of experience — breadth implausible at depth
No project descriptions, metrics, or outcomes anywhere in the resume
Job titles inflate from 'Intern' to 'Senior Engineer' within 18 months at the same company
screening_questions: Of the 14 technologies listed, which three have you used in production for more than six months?
Describe the most complex bug you fixed in the last year — what was the root cause?
Your title went from Intern to Senior in 18 months — what changed in your responsibilities?
candidates.submittal_draft: Not recommended for submittal in current form. If the screening call reveals genuine depth in 2-3 core technologies, consider repositioning the resume around those with concrete project evidence before any client introduction.

ranking_note: Submit Priya first — she clears the bar on both technical depth and leadership, and her red flags are conversational rather than disqualifying. Hold Marcus for a screening call: his profile pattern (team-credit language, missing specifics) often hides either a solid contributor with a weak resume or a passenger; ten minutes of pointed questions will tell you which. Do not submit Candidate 3 without a substantial rewrite and verification of actual production experience.
